verified_claims: The repository connects a retained MaleCNS graph to engineered ViZDoom visual inputs and fixed motor readouts.
Its experimental rule applies artificial damage input to two PPL101 cells and modifies selected KC-to-MBON11 weights.
limitations: The repository explicitly reports failed visual, conditioning and survival validation gates.
Artificial game damage is an engineering reinforcement signal, not a natural nociceptor model or pain label.
PPL101 and MBON11 are spectator readouts and learned survival has not been demonstrated.
decisions.corrected_purpose: Experimental MaleCNS-to-ViZDoom integration with explicit negative validation results and engineered reinforcement.
decisions.note: Retain as falsifiable implementation evidence; do not cite as successful learning, pain or whole-brain emulation.

verified_claims: The patent application describes ML processing of EEG features and embodiments combining EEG and ECAP-derived information for neurostimulation control.
It defines d_EEG from pain/paresthesia-related feature distances and an embodiment where d_total combines d_EEG with I_ECAP.
limitations: A patent application describes claimed embodiments and is not empirical validation, clinical efficacy evidence or a released algorithm.
Its pain-state EEG assumptions and combined metric require independent prospective validation.
decisions.corrected_purpose: Patent prior art for EEG/ECAP-informed machine-learning control of neurostimulation.
decisions.note: The imported equation is confirmed as an embodiment, not an established clinical method.

verified_claims: The granted patent describes neural stimulation and recording for closed-loop control.
One embodiment tunes an analog stimulation-artifact simulator and subtracts the artificial artifact before digital residual processing to extract ECAPs.
limitations: The patent is prior art, not validation of signal quality, clinical outcome or commercial implementation.
Artifact rejection does not turn ECAP into a direct measure of pain.
decisions.corrected_purpose: Granted patent prior art for simultaneous stimulation/recording and analog-plus-digital artifact rejection in ECAP sensing.
decisions.note: Exact B2 identifier and artifact-rejection embodiment were confirmed.

verified_claims: Brian2 is a free, open-source, clock-driven Python simulator for spiking neural networks.
It supports code generation, examples, tutorials and extensible neuron/synapse equations.
limitations: A general simulator does not provide a FlyWire, nociception or ECAP model by itself.
Project compatibility must be tested against the selected Python and accelerator stack.
decisions.corrected_purpose: General-purpose, equation-oriented SNN simulator and candidate reference CPU backend.
decisions.note: Software identity and maintained primary repository confirmed.

verified_claims: Brian2GeNN is a Brian2 backend interface for running supported models through GeNN on NVIDIA GPUs.
limitations: The maintainers label the software beta.
The imported 10-100x speedup is not a universal guarantee and was removed; performance depends on model and hardware.
The current GeNN project also supports AMD HIP, but Brian2GeNN's documented path is NVIDIA-focused.
decisions.corrected_purpose: Beta Brian2-to-GeNN backend for accelerator execution of supported SNN simulations.
decisions.note: Benchmark claims must be reproduced on the chosen whole-brain workload.

verified_claims: GeNN is a code-generation environment for neuronal-network simulation on NVIDIA CUDA and AMD HIP accelerators.
limitations: It is a simulation engine, not a biological model or dataset.
Supported model features and device memory limits require workload-specific testing.
decisions.corrected_purpose: GPU-accelerated neuronal-network simulation environment based on generated CUDA/HIP code.
decisions.note: Exact maintained repository replaces the former documentation-domain landing page.

verified_claims: NEST is an open-source simulator for the dynamics, size and structure of spiking neuronal networks.
It exposes Python and standalone interfaces and scales from laptops to compute clusters.
limitations: NEST focuses on network dynamics rather than exact single-neuron morphology.
No FlyWire, nociception or ECAP model is supplied by the framework itself.
decisions.corrected_purpose: Scalable point-neuron/network simulator and candidate independent backend for reproducibility checks.
decisions.note: Exact maintained repository and project scope confirmed.

verified_claims: sapicore is a public PyTorch-based framework for neuromorphic modeling with documentation and tutorials.
limitations: Repository metadata alone does not establish biological realism or suitability for a 100k-neuron connectome.
Activity is lower than the major general-purpose simulators and local execution has not been tested.
decisions.corrected_purpose: PyTorch-based neuromorphic-modeling framework for prototype comparison.
decisions.note: Retain as a candidate only after scale and reproducibility benchmarking.

searches.query: SNN Toolbox ANN to SNN official repository

verified_claims: The toolbox converts analog neural networks to spiking networks and runs them in supported spiking simulators.
limitations: Its primary use is ANN-to-SNN conversion, not connectome-constrained biological simulation.
The repository's last source push predates this audit by several years, so current dependency compatibility requires testing.
decisions.corrected_purpose: ANN-to-SNN conversion toolbox for deployment experiments, not a FlyBrain simulator.
decisions.note: Scope narrowed to the functionality stated by the repository.

verified_claims: Norse extends PyTorch with differentiable spiking-neuron components and provides notebooks, tasks and examples.
limitations: The library targets trainable deep SNNs and does not supply connectome or biological-validation data.
Repository performance statements are preliminary and workload-specific.
decisions.corrected_purpose: Differentiable PyTorch SNN component library for trainable baseline models and representation experiments.
decisions.note: Do not infer biological fidelity from bio-inspired components.

verified_claims: snnTorch provides gradient-based SNN learning integrated with PyTorch/autograd, surrogate gradients and NIR import/export.
limitations: It is a machine-learning library, not a biophysical connectome simulator.
GPU acceleration and feasible scale inherit PyTorch and require empirical benchmarking.
decisions.corrected_purpose: PyTorch library for gradient-based SNN baselines, training and interchange experiments.
decisions.note: Relevant to model comparison, not evidence for fly-to-human transfer.

verified_claims: The ACM article describes ModNEF as a modular open-source FPGA SNN emulator evaluated on a Xilinx Zynq device with MNIST/N-MNIST.
limitations: The imported GitHub organization URL returns 404 and no stable source repository was confirmed.
The paper does not establish support for whole-connectome scale, biological models or the project's target hardware.
decisions.corrected_purpose: Published FPGA SNN-emulator architecture whose reusable source location remains unverified.
decisions.note: Keep as hardware prior art, not as an immediately available implementation dependency.

verified_claims: MetaTF bundles Python packages for creating, converting, simulating and deploying networks on the Akida platform.
The official getting-started guide documents pip installation and a software simulator.
limitations: BrainChip states that examples are Apache-licensed but the underlying Akida library is proprietary under an EULA.
This is a deployment SDK and simulator, not open biological-neural simulation software.
decisions.corrected_purpose: Proprietary-core Akida development framework with Python APIs, conversion tools and a software simulator.
decisions.note: Licensing must be reviewed before reproducible dissertation artifacts depend on it.

searches.query: BrainChip Edge AI Box official product brief

verified_claims: The official product brief describes an Edge AI Box with an NXP i.MX 8M Plus and two AKD1000 accelerators.
limitations: The checked Edge AI Box is AKD1000-based; the imported AKD1000/AKD1500 wording was not confirmed.
It is commercial deployment hardware, not required for dataset or simulator validity.
decisions.corrected_purpose: Commercial AKD1000 Edge AI Box for Akida edge-inference demonstrations.
decisions.note: Hardware purchase is optional and must follow a measured software-only feasibility comparison.

verified_claims: BrainChip markets AKD1500 silicon and PCIe/M.2 evaluation hardware and publishes example projects in DevHub.
The official material states that tools/model examples are available without subscription fees.
limitations: AKD1500 hardware and the underlying Akida runtime are not established as open-source; the imported label is false as written.
No Arduino Nicla driver claim was verified for AKD1500.
decisions.corrected_purpose: Commercial AKD1500 neuromorphic accelerator with public examples and proprietary runtime components.
decisions.note: Do not describe the chip or complete software stack as open-source.
